subject: SOC 2 / ISO mapping: RBAC v2 deliverables -> control evidence needed (March audit window)
body:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kaitlyn Nguyen <kaitlyn.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Mar 6, 2025 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: SOC 2 / ISO mapping: RBAC v2 deliverables -> control evidence needed (March audit window)

Hi Marcus + Kevin,

We’re in the March audit window with AssureTrust and I’m mapping RBAC v2 deliverables to SOC 2 (Security / Confidentiality) + ISO27001 evidence asks.

I started a control mapping worksheet (attached) and need help filling the “Evidence artifacts” column with concrete items we can hand over (screenshots/log samples/links) vs. just design intent.

Top evidence asks we need to satisfy:
1) Access control enforcement: proof RBAC checks are consistently applied on control plane + console backend.
2) Separation of duties: default roles, role assignment flows, and restrictions (billing vs security vs support).
3) Auditability: authorization decisions logged with actor, role, allow/deny, policy version, reason.
4) Break-glass/impersonation: time-bounded elevated access + monitoring/approvals.
5) Change management: how new sensitive actions are reviewed and tested (governance/CI checks).

Can you or your teams provide:
- A sample audit log event showing the new authz decision fields (ideally allow + deny examples).
- Links to the Confluence overview + role definition pages (stable URLs).
- Anything we can point to for governance (e.g., CI gate requiring permission annotation).
- For break-glass: runbook link + what audit evidence we retain (who approved, time bounds, alerting).

Attachment: RBACv2_SOC2-ISO_Control_Mapping_v1.xlsx

Thanks,
Olga

—
Olga Petrov
GRC Lead, Redwood Inference



From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Kaitlyn Nguyen <kaitlyn.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Mar 6, 2025 at 10:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: SOC 2 / ISO mapping: RBAC v2 deliverables -> control evidence needed (March audit window)

Olga,

Yes. We can support. A few quick pointers (Kevin/Kaitlyn will add specifics):

- RBAC v2 overview + terminology: confluence://security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/rbac-v2-overview
- Default roles matrix + separation-of-duties notes: confluence://security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/rbac-v2-role-definitions
- Methodology for permission inventory + sensitivity rubric (P0/P1/P2): confluence://security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/permission-inventory-methodology

Governance/engineering enforcement:
- Conformance test suite / CI enforcement that endpoints declare permission + check is wired: github://redwood/pr_18633

Break-glass plumbing is in flight but we have the runbook and audit event plan. I’ll let Kaitlyn + Kevin provide details and sample artifacts.

Marcus

—
Marcus Lin
Security Engineering (Exec Owner), Redwood Inference



From: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kaitlyn Nguyen <kaitlyn.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Mar 7, 2025 at 8:26 AM PST
Subject: Re: SOC 2 / ISO mapping: RBAC v2 deliverables -> control evidence needed (March audit window)

Olga,

For auditability evidence, the canonical spec is here: confluence://security-and-compliance/audit-logging/authz-decision-audit-logging

Implementation references you can cite:
- Audit log enrichment PR (adds policy_version, role_ids, decision_reason, etc.): github://redwood/pr_18522
- Exporter compatibility PR for SIEM targets (keeps backward compat): github://audit-log-exporter/pr_88

Concrete artifacts I can provide by Monday:
- 2 sample audit log events (allow + deny) with authz decision context
- A “schema excerpt” (field list) we can share externally

One note for the worksheet: we should map this to SOC2 CC6.1/CC6.2 and CC7.2 (monitoring/alerting on privileged access), and to ISO27001 Annex A controls around access control + logging.

Kevin

—
Kevin Osei
Audit Logging Lead, Redwood Inference



From: Kaitlyn Nguyen <kaitlyn.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Mar 7, 2025 at 11:04 AM PST
Subject: Re: SOC 2 / ISO mapping: RBAC v2 deliverables -> control evidence needed (March audit window)

Olga,

On “consistent enforcement” + change management:

1) Enforcement standard (where checks happen + testing expectations):
- confluence://architecture-and-standards/api-standards/authz-check-standard

2) Policy format ADR (useful for auditors to understand versioning semantics):
- confluence://architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-014-rbac-v2-policy-format

3) Rollout/migration (dual-eval, shadow-deny metrics, flags):
- confluence://security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/rbac-v2-migration-plan
- Implementation refs: github://redwood/pr_18579

4) Evidence we can generate:
- Screenshot of our “shadow-deny” dashboard w/ metrics (RBACv1 allowed but v2 would deny), with timestamps.
- CI check screenshot/log showing PR failing when endpoint is missing permission annotation (from github://redwood/pr_18633).

I’ll coordinate with Connor to get “nice” screenshots that don’t expose customer-specific identifiers.

Kaitlyn

—
Kaitlyn Nguyen
AuthZ Implementation Lead, Platform Control Plane



From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@assuretrust.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 2:18 PM PDT
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence planning — RBAC v2 / authorization auditability

Hi Evan,

Ahead of our evidence request list, here’s what Redwood will provide this week for RBAC v2 (authorization):

- RBAC v2 overview + default roles matrix (separation of duties)
- Audit log examples showing authorization decision context (allow + deny)
- Engineering governance evidence (CI gate requiring permission declarations/tests)
- Break-glass/impersonation runbook + example audit records for elevated access sessions

We’ll package these in a single evidence bundle and label which SOC 2 criteria and ISO controls each item supports.

If you have preferred formats (e.g., redacted screenshots vs. PDFs), let me know.

Best,
Olga

—
Olga Petrov
GRC Lead, Redwood Inference



From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@assuretrust.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 11, 2025 at 9:03 AM PDT
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence planning — RBAC v2 / authorization auditability

Hi Olga,

Thanks — screenshots or PDF exports are fine. For the audit logs, JSON examples are ideal as long as they’re clearly redacted and include:

- Unique event ID
- Actor identity (can be pseudonymized) + role/permission used
- Resource/action attempted
- Allow/deny outcome and reason
- Timestamp and system/component

For break-glass, we’ll look for:
- Approval mechanism
- Time-bounded access
- Monitoring/alerts for use

Regards,
Evan Brooks
Senior Auditor, AssureTrust LLP



From: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kaitlyn Nguyen <kaitlyn.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 11, 2025 at 1:37 PM PDT
Subject: Re: SOC 2 / ISO mapping: RBAC v2 deliverables -> control evidence needed (March audit window)

Olga,

As promised, attaching redacted JSONL examples (1 allow + 1 deny) that show the authz decision context.

Attachment: AuditLog_authz_decision_sample_v0.1.jsonl

Notes for the worksheet:
- The “deny” example includes decision_reason="missing_permission" + required_permission="org.sso.update".
- policy_version is included as a semantic version string (e.g., "rbac_bundle_v0.1.3").
- role_ids is a list in the internal schema; for external evidence we can show it as a comma-separated string if needed.

Also, the spec includes the full field list and retention considerations (what’s required vs optional) here:
confluence://security-and-compliance/audit-logging/authz-decision-audit-logging

Kevin



From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kaitlyn Nguyen <kaitlyn.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Mar 12, 2025 at 10:22 AM PDT
Subject: Re: SOC 2 / ISO mapping: RBAC v2 deliverables -> control evidence needed (March audit window)

Olga,

Attached are sanitized UI screenshots for role assignment + warning banners in the Console (current staging build). These show:
- Default roles list (Org Admin, Billing Admin, Security Admin, Developer, Read-only)
- Separation-of-duties copy (billing can’t change SSO; security can’t change invoices)
- “High risk permission” warning pattern when granting Security Admin

Attachment: Console_RoleAssignment_UI_screenshots_2025-03-11.zip

Break-glass / support impersonation:
- Runbook + evidence checklist doc attached (internal only; you can excerpt redacted portions for the auditor)
- Implementation ref (time-bounded elevated session + audit events): github://redwood/pr_18560

Attachment: BreakGlass_Runbook_EvidenceChecklist_v2.docx

Connor

—
Connor O’Brien
Release/Migration Lead, Redwood Inference



From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Kaitlyn Nguyen <kaitlyn.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Mar 12, 2025 at 4:47 PM PDT
Subject: Re: SOC 2 / ISO mapping: RBAC v2 deliverables -> control evidence needed (March audit window)

Marcus / Aisha,

I’ve incorporated the artifacts into the control mapping sheet. Two items need a decision/confirmation for the auditor narrative:

1) Support impersonation for Private customers
- Current stance in the runbook implies “disabled by default” + explicit customer opt-in.
- Can we confirm that’s the policy statement we want in the SOC 2 description? (Evan will ask.)

2) Break-glass approvals
- The checklist references Security on-call + incident commander approval for production use.
- Aisha: do we want to codify this as a “must” vs “should” for audit language? (I’m leaning must.)

If you both agree, I’ll finalize the evidence bundle for AssureTrust and schedule a 20-min walkthrough.

Olga

—
Olga Petrov
GRC Lead, Redwood Inference
